```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Setup: read the simulation outputs"
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = knitr::is_html_output())
options(knitr.kable.NA = "—")
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

inputs = readRDS(file.path("data", "om-inputs.rds"))
det    = readRDS(file.path("data", "deterministic.rds"))
se     = readRDS(file.path("data", "sim-est.rds"))
traj   = as.data.table(det$traj)
res    = as.data.table(se$results)
n_t    = inputs$n_t

fmt = function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
pct = function(x, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%")

om_lab = c(age = "age-based truth (SS3 curves)", length = "length-based truth (C2 curves)")
em_lab = c(age = "age", length_c2 = "length (C2 parameters)", length_all = "length (all parameters)")
em_col = c("age" = "#D35400", "length (C2 parameters)" = "#1E8449", "length (all parameters)" = "#8E44AD")
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
          theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
term = traj[ts == n_t]
g = function(cv, k = 1) term[curve == cv & mult == k, dep]
```

# Why this matters

In the IO yellowfin conversion, opal with SS3's age-based selectivity held
fixed (fit A1) reproduced SS3's stock size: B0 1.03 × SS3's and terminal
depletion 0.404 against SS3's 0.399. When opal estimated its own
length-based selectivity instead (fits C and C2), B0 fell to 0.88 × SS3's
and terminal depletion to 0.307. The [timing simulation](../timing/timing-sim.qmd)
showed that catch and biology timing barely move estimated depletion, which
leaves selectivity as the main candidate.

SS3's curves for this model are **age-based**: selectivity is a function of
age, and every fish of an age is equally selected whatever its length.
opal's are **length-based**: selectivity is a function of length, and
reaches age through the distribution of length at age. Two consequences:

1. The same curve family produces different shapes of selectivity-at-age,
   so one cannot reproduce the other exactly.
2. Length-based selection also changes the predicted length composition
   *within* an age: larger fish of an age are more likely to be caught. An
   age-based model predicts the catch's lengths from the population's
   length distribution at age alone.

This document tests whether these differences bias B0 and depletion, using
the model of the timing simulation with opal's timing conventions
(start-of-quarter catch and biology) throughout, so that only selectivity
differs.

# Design

## True selectivity

```{r}
#| label: rmse
r = inputs$sel$rmse
knitr::kable(data.table(fishery = r$fishery,
                        `age truth vs SS3` = r$age_truth_vs_ss3,
                        `length approximation of age truth` = r$length_approx_of_age,
                        `age approximation of length truth` = r$age_approx_of_length),
             digits = 4, caption = "RMSE of selectivity-at-age (ages 1–28) for each fit.")
```

* **Age-based truth:** opal's double-normal curve evaluated on age (the same
  six-parameter form as SS3's pattern 20), fitted by least squares to SS3's
  selectivity-at-age for the source fleets of the three pooled fisheries
  (SS3 fleets 11, 4 and 8). It reproduces SS3's curves almost exactly.
* **Length-based truth:** C2's fitted length-based curves for the same
  fleets, as in the timing simulation.
* **Cross-approximations:** each truth fitted by least squares in the other
  basis, on selectivity-at-age. This is the step C2 used to seed opal's
  curves from SS3's. A length-based curve approximates the age-based truth
  worse than the reverse: an age-based curve can bend at any age, while a
  length-based one is smoothed by the spread of length at age.

```{r}
#| label: sel-curves
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Selectivity-at-age of each truth and its approximation in the other basis, with SS3's curves (orange circles)."
sa = as.data.table(det$sel_age)
sa[, truth_f := factor(om_lab[truth], om_lab)]
ss3 = as.data.table(inputs$sel$ss3_sel_age)
ss3[, fishery := inputs$fleet_names[match(fishery, c(11, 4, 8))]]
ss3[, truth_f := factor(om_lab["age"], om_lab)]
ggplot(sa, aes(age, sel, colour = curve, linetype = curve)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(data = ss3, aes(age, sel), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.4, shape = 1, colour = "#D35400") +
    facet_grid(truth_f ~ fishery) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("age truth" = "grey20", "length approximation" = "#1E8449",
                                   "length truth" = "#1E8449", "age approximation" = "grey20"), name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("age truth" = "solid", "length approximation" = "dashed",
                                     "length truth" = "solid", "age approximation" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Selectivity")
```

## Simulation–estimation

Each of `r se$n_rep` replicates draws recruitment deviations (shared by both
operating models) and observation error, with the timing simulation's data:
a longline index (CV `r inputs$index_cv`, quarters
`r min(inputs$index_t)`–`r max(inputs$index_t)`), multinomial length
compositions (ESS `r inputs$comp_ess`) for each fishery in every quarter
with catch, and catch known exactly. Three estimation models fit each
dataset:

| Estimation model | Basis | Estimated selectivity columns |
|---|---|---|
| `age` | age | 1–4 (peak, plateau, ascending and descending width) for all three fisheries, as SS3 estimated |
| `length (C2 parameters)` | length | C2's choices: 1–4, and 1 and 3 for the longline |
| `length (all parameters)` | length | 1–4 for all fisheries, plus 5–6 (initial and final selectivity) for the two dome-shaped fisheries |

All estimate log B0, `r n_t` recruitment deviations (N(0, σ~R~) penalty)
and log q, and put opal's N(0, 2) prior on the estimated selectivity
parameters. Unestimated selectivity columns stay at their starting values:
the truth when the basis matches the operating model, otherwise the
least-squares approximation, as in C2. Fits start at the true B0, q and
recruitment deviations, and are polished with Newton steps.

As in the timing simulation, recruitment-deviation shrinkage biases even
the matched models (B0 up, depletion down), so each model is also compared
**paired against the matched model on the same dataset**: `age` for the
age-based truth, `length (C2 parameters)` for the length-based truth.

# Part 1: the same parameters, the other basis

Each truth is projected with its approximation in the other basis, with the
same B0, recruitment and catch. Nothing is estimated.

```{r}
#| label: det-table
tab = dcast(term, truth + mult ~ curve, value.var = "dep")
tab = rbind(tab[truth == "age", .(truth = om_lab["age"], mult, truth_dep = `age truth`, approx = `length approximation`)],
            tab[truth == "length", .(truth = om_lab["length"], mult, truth_dep = `length truth`, approx = `age approximation`)])
tab[, diff := pct(approx / truth_dep - 1, 1)]
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 3,
             col.names = c("Truth", "Catch ×", "Terminal SSB/B0, truth", "with the other basis' approximation", "Difference"))
```

With the same B0, recruitment and catch, swapping a truth for its best
approximation in the other basis changes terminal depletion little: at the
observed catch, `r fmt(g("age truth"), 3)` for the age-based truth against
`r fmt(g("length approximation"), 3)` with its length-based approximation
(`r pct(g("length approximation") / g("age truth") - 1, 1)`), and
`r fmt(g("length truth"), 3)` against `r fmt(g("age approximation"), 3)`
for the length-based truth
(`r pct(g("age approximation") / g("length truth") - 1, 1)`). The
difference grows with the catch but stays small next to the timing effects.
So the shapes alone are not the issue; any larger effect has to come from
how the curves are estimated against the length compositions.

# Part 2: estimating selectivity in each basis

```{r}
#| label: fit-quality
fq = res[, .(fits = .N, failed = sum(is.na(B0)), `max |gradient| (max)` = max(max_gradient, na.rm = TRUE),
             `seconds (median)` = median(seconds, na.rm = TRUE))]
knitr::kable(fq, digits = 4, caption = "Fit diagnostics over all fits.")
```

```{r}
#| label: est-prep
res[, `:=`(rel_B0 = B0 / B0_true - 1, err_dep = dep_T - dep_T_true,
           em_f = factor(em_lab[em], em_lab), om_f = factor(om_lab[om], om_lab))]
res[, matched := (om == "age" & em == "age") | (om == "length" & em == "length_c2")]
ref = res[matched == TRUE, .(rep, om, ref_B0 = B0, ref_dep = dep_T)]
res = merge(res, ref, by = c("rep", "om"))
res[, `:=`(paired_B0 = B0 / ref_B0 - 1, paired_dep = dep_T - ref_dep)]
```

```{r}
#| label: est-box
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Relative error in B0 (top) and error in terminal depletion (bottom) by estimation model, for each operating model."
long = rbind(res[, .(om_f, em_f, value = rel_B0, what = "B0: relative error")],
             res[, .(om_f, em_f, value = err_dep, what = "terminal SSB/B0: error")])
ggplot(long, aes(em_f, value, fill = em_f)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6, width = 0.6) +
    facet_grid(what ~ om_f, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = em_col, name = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank()) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: est-table
smry = res[, .(B0_err = pct(median(rel_B0), 1), B0_vs = pct(median(paired_B0), 1),
               dep_err = fmt(median(err_dep), 3), dep_vs = fmt(median(paired_dep), 3),
               dep_vs_iqr = paste(fmt(quantile(paired_dep, 0.25), 3), "to", fmt(quantile(paired_dep, 0.75), 3)),
               mare = fmt(mean(mare_dep), 3)),
           by = .(om = sub(" truth.*", "", om_lab[om]), em = paste0(em_lab[em], ifelse(matched, " *", "")))]
knitr::kable(smry[order(om, em)],
             col.names = c("Truth", "Estimation model", "B0 error", "B0 vs matched", "Term. dep. error",
                           "Term. dep. vs matched", "IQR vs matched", "Mean abs. dep. error"),
             caption = "Medians over replicates (mean for the last column). 'vs matched' is the paired difference from the matched estimation model (*) on the same dataset.")
```

```{r}
#| label: est-sel
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Estimated selectivity-at-age (median and 10–90% range over replicates) against the truth (black)."
es = as.data.table(se$sel)[, .(med = median(sel), lo = quantile(sel, 0.1), hi = quantile(sel, 0.9)),
                           by = .(om, em, fishery, age)]
es[, `:=`(em_f = factor(em_lab[em], em_lab), om_f = factor(om_lab[om], om_lab))]
tr = sa[curve %in% c("age truth", "length truth")]
tr[, om_f := factor(om_lab[truth], om_lab)]
ggplot(es, aes(age, med, colour = em_f, fill = em_f)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_line(data = tr, aes(age, sel), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
    facet_grid(om_f ~ fishery) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = em_col, name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = em_col, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Age (quarters)", y = "Selectivity")
```

```{r}
#| label: est-numbers
q = function(o, e, v) res[om == o & em == e, median(get(v))]
qq = function(o, e, v, p) res[om == o & em == e, quantile(get(v), p)]
```

All `r nrow(res)` fits converged (largest gradient
`r formatC(max(res$max_gradient), format = "e", digits = 1)`).

**A length-based model fitted to age-based data keeps depletion.** With
SS3-like age-based selectivity as the truth, the length-based models
estimate B0 `r pct(q("age", "length_c2", "paired_B0"), 1)` (C2 parameters)
to `r pct(q("age", "length_all", "paired_B0"), 1)` (all parameters) higher
than the matched age-based model, but terminal depletion within
`r fmt(abs(q("age", "length_c2", "paired_dep")), 3)`
(10–90%: `r fmt(qq("age", "length_c2", "paired_dep", 0.1), 3)` to
`r fmt(qq("age", "length_c2", "paired_dep", 0.9), 3)`). As with timing, the
misspecification goes into the scale.

**An age-based model fitted to length-based data does not.** With opal-like
length-based selectivity as the truth, the age-based model estimates
terminal depletion `r fmt(abs(q("length", "age", "paired_dep")), 3)` lower
than the matched model (10–90%: `r fmt(qq("length", "age", "paired_dep", 0.1), 3)`
to `r fmt(qq("length", "age", "paired_dep", 0.9), 3)`), and B0
`r pct(abs(q("length", "age", "paired_B0")), 1)` lower: the stock looks
more depleted than it is. An age-based model cannot represent the larger
fish of each age being caught preferentially, so it misfits the catch's
length compositions and absorbs the difference in the stock's trajectory.

**Estimating more length-based parameters changes little.** Freeing the
initial and final selectivity of the dome-shaped fisheries
(`length (all parameters)`) moves terminal depletion by
`r fmt(abs(q("length", "length_all", "paired_dep")), 3)` (length truth) and
`r fmt(abs(q("age", "length_all", "paired_dep") - q("age", "length_c2", "paired_dep")), 3)`
(age truth) relative to C2's parameter choices.

**The direction does not match the IO yellowfin fits.** In those fits, opal's
length-based selectivity (C2) gave a *lower* B0 (0.88 against 1.03 × SS3's
with SS3's selectivity) and *lower* depletion (0.307 against 0.404) than
SS3's age-based curves. Here, fitted to the same data, the length-based
model's B0 and depletion are at or above the age-based model's in the
median: B0 is
`r pct(res[, .(d = B0[em == "length_c2"] / B0[em == "age"] - 1), by = .(rep, om)][, median(d)], 1)`
higher and terminal depletion
`r fmt(res[om == "age", .(d = dep_T[em == "length_c2"] - dep_T[em == "age"]), by = rep][, median(d)], 3)`
(age truth) to
`r fmt(res[om == "length", .(d = dep_T[em == "length_c2"] - dep_T[em == "age"]), by = rep][, median(d)], 3)`
(length truth) higher. The selectivity basis on its own therefore does not
explain C2's lower stock size.

# Implications for opal

1. **Length-based selectivity is the safer default.** When the truth is
   age-based, opal's length-based curves still estimate depletion without
   bias (B0 is about 4–6% high). When the truth is length-based, an
   age-based model biases depletion low. An option for age-based curves
   would help reproduce SS3 models exactly, but is not needed for unbiased
   status estimates.
2. **The IO yellowfin gap is not a basis effect.** Both simulations (timing
   and selectivity) move estimated depletion by at most about 0.04, and
   in the opposite direction to C2's lower depletion (0.307 against
   SS3's 0.399). The remaining candidates are features these simulations
   leave out:
   * the full set of 16 fleets, with fleet-specific shapes that a
     length-based double normal fits poorly (for example fishery 5's
     shallow ascending limb and fishery 9's drop in the plus group);
   * the survey's generalised size-frequency data, which SS3 fitted and the
     converter omits, leaving the index selectivity weakly informed;
   * opal's N(0, 2) prior on the selectivity parameters, which set nine of
     C's parameters;
   * data from a spatial operating model, where pooled area fleets need not
     follow either basis.
   A next step would be to rerun this design with all 16 fleets, or to
   refit C2 with the survey's size-frequency data, to see which of these
   moves depletion by 0.1.
3. **Freeing more selectivity parameters is not the fix.** Estimating the
   initial and final selectivity of the domes made almost no difference.

# Reproducing

| Step | Script | Does | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `01-om-inputs.r` | True and approximating selectivity curves; reuses `../timing/data/om-inputs.rds` | ~10 s |
| 2 | `02-deterministic.r` | Part 1 projections | ~10 s |
| 3 | `03-sim-est.r [n_rep] [n_cores]` | Part 2, `r se$n_rep` replicates × 6 fits | `r fmt(se$minutes, 0)` min on 4 cores |
| 4 | `selectivity-sim.qmd` | This document; reads only `data/` | seconds |

The model is the timing simulation's (`../timing/R/timing-model.R`), which
gained a `sel_basis` argument for this study. Results were generated
`r se$created`.
